## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

- **Date:** 2026-07-20  
  **Source:** [AP — Moonshot AI halts new Kimi K3 subscriptions](https://apnews.com/article/kimi-k3-china-ai-model-us-4c66a2e0f557ce79d3cc2d769c9a6226)  
  **Summary:** AP reported Moonshot temporarily paused new consumer subscriptions for Kimi K3 after demand over 48 hours pushed the company near current compute limits. Existing subscribers reportedly retain access while Moonshot expands capacity and reopens slots in batches.  
  **Why it matters:** Capacity constraints are now an operational signal for frontier-app demand in China, not just a model-quality story.

- **Date:** 2026-07-20  
  **Source:** [OpenAI — Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models](https://openai.com/index/safety-alignment-long-horizon-models)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI published deployment lessons for long-running AI models, focusing on safety risks, observed failures, and iterative safeguards for models operating over longer time horizons.  
  **Why it matters:** Long-horizon autonomy increases the importance of monitoring, interruption, recovery, and adversarial testing as deployment controls, not just pre-release evaluation.

## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics

- **Date:** 2026-07-20  
  **Source:** [YouTube — From Zero to Your First Agentic AI Workflow in 26 Minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDGiWn0flK8)  
  **Summary:** A high-view tutorial shows a basic agentic workflow using Claude Code-style project context, task instructions, and iterative execution.  
  **How to use:** Define the target outcome, add project-specific instructions, give the agent a bounded task, inspect diffs/output, then iterate with corrective prompts.  
  **Availability:** Available now, assuming access to Claude Code or equivalent agentic coding tools.  
  **Why it matters:** The practical pattern is reproducible: scoped tasking plus fast review loops, not broad autonomous delegation.

- **Date:** 2026-07-20  
  **Source:** [YouTube — How I Use Claude Cowork to Automate 99% Of My Life](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cJ2QCyr3yzU)  
  **Summary:** The video describes personal workflow automation around Claude Cowork-style assistants, but the source notes recent Claude changes may affect plugin behavior.  
  **How to use:** Treat this as a pattern lead only: inventory recurring tasks, connect the relevant automation surface, test one low-risk workflow, and verify output manually before expanding.  
  **Availability:** Partially available; plugin compatibility is uncertain from the supplied source.  
  **Why it matters:** Workflow automation claims are high-noise; the usable takeaway is to start with narrow, reversible automations.
